subject: CTC discovery: fit validation + post-update guardrails
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@ctc-fin.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: artifacts + recommended next steps

Hi Claire — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the artifacts we promised attached.

What we covered (short):
- Primary use case: transaction categorization + entity extraction for merchant dispute flows.
- Latency target: P95 < 250ms for single-request classification.
- Quality target: precision >= 95% on labeled GoldenSet for merchants/amounts.

Attached for your team: ctc_eval_pack_v1.zip (benchmarks + golden prompts), prompt_set_ctc_v2.jsonl (production prompt templates), diff_report_20280325.pdf (recent model delta summary).

Suggested immediate steps:
1) Start a 1-week canary driving 5% traffic to the recommended model variant (details below).
2) Freeze production snapshot and pin to a stable variant if you want immediate rollback ability.
3) Run the goldenset on the canary and alert on these metrics: precision, recall, hallucination rate (free-text entity hallucinations), and average latency.

Model recommendations (based on today's demo workload):
- Redwood-XL-1.2 (float16) — highest quality baseline.
- Redwood-Large-v1.3-q4_0 — preferred for cost/latency tradeoff in throughput scenarios; we observed similar precision on sampled prompts but ~20% lower token cost.

Important caveat: our internal pre-release notes flagged a small regression after the 2028-03-25 model rollout that increases free-text hallucination for certain short-prefix prompts (we include the diff report). For safety, we recommend pinning production to the 2028-03-24 snapshot until the canary validates.

Next steps from our side:
- Camila: deliver artifacts (done, attached) and set up the Console canary template.
- Priyom: provide the evaluation checklist and what to monitor.

Happy to hop on a 20-min sync tomorrow if your eng/security teams want to walk through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

-- Attachment(s): ctc_eval_pack_v1.zip (archive), prompt_set_ctc_v2.jsonl (jsonl), diff_report_20280325.pdf (report)

2) If we pin to 2028-03-24, what is the process and SLA for rollback if the canary shows a problem?

Security will also want to review the prompt_set and the goldenset before we run anything in prod. Can you also share a read-only link to the evaluation artifacts?

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-demo: artifacts + recommended next steps

Priyom / Priya — forwarding Claire's questions. My replies inline below (keeps thread for audit):

On Mon, Mar 27, 2028 at 5:08 PM Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@ctc-fin.com> wrote:
> Thanks Camila — this is helpful. A couple quick questions before we kick off anything: 
> 1) The regression note is concerning. Can you quantify the delta on hallucination rate and whether it affects merchant extraction specifically?
>
> 2) If we pin to 2028-03-24, what is the process and SLA for rollback if the canary shows a problem?
>
> Security will also want to review the prompt_set and the goldenset before we run anything in prod. Can you also share a read-only link to the evaluation artifacts?

My answers: 
1) Quantified delta: on our internal goldenset used for transaction extraction, hallucination rate (free-text merchant extractions that are not in-source) increased from 0.8% -> 2.9% comparing 2028-03-24 -> 2028-03-25 on the short-prefix set (prompts under 30 chars). Precision on merchant labels dropped 95.4% -> 92.1% in that slice. The attached diff_report_20280325.pdf has the sample cases and comparison table.

2) Pin & rollback process:
- We create a production snapshot (Console: Snapshots > Create) and then apply a pin to the snapshot ID. Pin provides immediate routing to the pinned model variant.
- SLA: we can remove the pin and re-route to a fallback variant within 15 minutes (manual unpin). For guaranteed automated rollback we recommend a canary monitor with thresholds and an on-call runbook; if thresholds are breached we can push a rollback within 30 minutes.

Recommend operational plan for CTC:
A) Start a 5% canary to Redwood-Large-v1.3-q4_0 for 24 hours with the goldenset run every 2 hours.
B) Keep production pinned to 2028-03-24 snapshot for initial safety.
C) If canary metrics show <= 0.5% absolute drop in precision vs pinned baseline AND hallucination rate remains <1.5%, then unpin and roll to v1.3 for gradual ramp.

I've uploaded a read-only artifact bundle to Drive and linked it in the related_links above.

Attachments: diff_report_20280325.pdf — contains the flagged examples and the measured deltas.

Can you take point on coordinating the pin (Priyom) and the security readout (Priya)? I can send a short checklist to Claire's team.

Thanks,
Camila
